commits.message: test(style): pin SGR parameter order where it is decided, against Rich's bytes (rich-color-7kv)

fix(style): a combined style writes attributes before colours, as Rich does (rich-color-7kv)

Style.toSgrCodes wrote foreground, background, then attributes; Rich
9d8f9a3's _make_ansi_codes writes attributes, then foreground, then
background. `[bold red]x[/]` is now `\e[1;31m`, byte-identical to the
reference.

The markup golden gains two reference-generated cases that put
attributes and colours in one style, and the pinned-divergence test
that stood in for them is gone. The two printJson highlight tests now
pin Rich's own bytes instead of a restyled RichText.

fix(widgets): a widget owns its rectangle; drags follow the repainted widget; releases know if they landed (rich-runtime-fna.2)

- WidgetBase.render pads every row to the widest and terminates each row,
  so a click past a short row still hits and a blank last row survives.
- Captured drags read the widget's origin off the current frame (originOf).
- WidgetMouseEvent carries `over`; the parser's event is ScreenMouseEvent.
  Dropdown reads `over` instead of recomputing its own extent.
- Segment.anchorLines takes firstRow; the overlay pass drops its pad/slice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(widgets): hit-test the painted frame; widgets get their own coordinates (rich-runtime-fna.2)

WidgetBase.render stamps a subclass's `draw` output with its anchor, so the
frame a screen paints is its own hit map. `widgetAt(frame, x, y)` names the
innermost widget under a cell and the cell's place in that widget's output;
EventRouter reads it off `FrameSource.frame` and delivers each pointer event
in the widget's own coordinates, a captured drag relative to the origin its
press found. `bounds`, `WidgetBounds`, `containsPoint`, the active-overlay
set and the z-sorted `widgets` getter are gone: z-order is paint order, and
the overlay pass stamps overlay row i as the widget's row footprint+i.

refactor(segment)!: two bounding primitives, named; Table splits through the one (rich-segment-bpa) (#193)

* refactor(segment): two bounding primitives, named; Table splits through the one (rich-segment-bpa)

cropLines keeps a stream's line structure and bounds it; splitAndCropLines
decomposes into rows of exactly the width. segment.ts now says which question
each answers. Table's hand-rolled splitLines+adjustLineLength is the second
one, so it calls it. splitAndCropLines' pad/includeNewLines/style modes had no
caller and are gone.

* review(segment): one blank-cell rule in Table; header places Tree; pin the split's edges (rich-segment-bpa)
